title: Endpoint modular moment to energy Cauchy bridge
question: Can the endpoint modular-frequency moment isolated by R-380 be converted exactly to a Gibbs energy-difference first moment and bounded by a quadratic state-weighted energy-commutator moment?
method: Use the actual-Q3 edge and square finite fixtures with all translated sites and bond terms, both term orders, both time signs, every prefix position and both history adjoints on the declared cutoffs.
Diagonalize each doubled bond generator, construct normalized Gibbs probabilities and center every moved Hermitian witness in the same bond-Gibbs state.
Compute the endpoint modular moment in both eigenvalue orientations, convert it to beta times the absolute energy-difference first moment, and compute M_0 and M_2 with the same state weight.
Check the exact Gibbs log-energy identity, left/right moment symmetry, endpoint reconstruction, positivity and the state-weighted Cauchy envelope D_1<=beta sqrt(M_0 M_2).
Rebuild the same finite grid in a non-importing independent lane and formalize the scalar square-root Cauchy envelope in Lean R381.
finding: The primary lane passes 17,931/17,931 assertions and the non-importing independent lane passes 11/11 aggregate assertions over 2,560 all-prefix actual-Q3 contexts. The integrated verifier passes 61/61 and Lean R381 compiles. Primary and independent numerical fields agree within 1.918465386552270e-13. The largest endpoint modular moment is 2.15358381458932, the largest state-weighted M_0 is 41.64826651661874, the largest M_2 is 17.719559304500326, and the largest Cauchy envelope is 27.165951639338186. The maximum endpoint-to-Cauchy ratio is 0.07927511037274983 and the maximum Cauchy violation is -2.290857218268337e-16.
decision_reason: The Gibbs log-energy identity turns the R-380 endpoint into a first energy-difference moment, and finite state-weighted Cauchy bounds it by a quadratic energy-commutator moment. The finite envelope is loose but valid, so the next obstruction is a uniform common-core estimate for M_0 and M_2 rather than the algebraic conversion itself. This is a route-local finite result, not a QFT promotion.

adversarial_review.check: Partition and energy-shift terms cancel in the logarithmic difference on every finite spectrum.
The endpoint retains |E_i-E_j| without assuming an eigenvalue ordering.
The inequality is tested one-sided as D_1<=beta sqrt(M_0 M_2); no equality is asserted.
Both p_i and p_j orientations are computed and compared using Hermitian entry symmetry.
Only energy differences enter M_2, so the numerical stabilization shift cannot change the identity.
The witness remains a full matrix in the bond-Hamiltonian eigenbasis; rho is never commuted through X.
Diagonal and degenerate entries remain in the sums and contribute zero without singular division.
M_0, M_2 and endpoint values remain finite-grid diagnostics and are not promoted to uniform bounds.
The independent lane rebuilds oscillator, graph, spectrum, prefixes and moments without importing the primary audit.
No common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A conclusion is drawn.

next_action: Establish a source-local uniform estimate for M_0 and M_2 on the Hamiltonian-derived common core, then insert the endpoint bound into the R-380 interpolation and R-377 resolvent telescope.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite endpoint-energy Cauchy interface only. It does not prove source/volume/cutoff/beta uniformity, modular tails, common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A.
no_overclaim: R-381 identifies a quadratic energy-moment premise for the endpoint debt; it is not a uniform theorem or a QFT closure.
